priorStories.headline: S&P 500 enters correction; Nasdaq falls 5.3%
priorStories.body:
The S&P 500 fell 3.7% Friday, closing more than 10% below its October 6 record—a decline known as a correction. The index lost 8.6% over the week.

The Nasdaq composite dropped 5.3%, leaving it down for the year. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.9%.

priorStories.headline: Poland reports Russian missiles and drone entering airspace
priorStories.body:
Polish officials said three Russian objects entered the country's airspace and came down in southeastern Poland on Friday. They were believed to be two missiles and a jet-powered drone, though their identification remained preliminary.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as an apparent intentional provocation. It coincided with European military exercises for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.

priorStories.headline: Man convicted of starting deadly Palisades Fire
priorStories.body:
A federal jury convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht on Friday of destruction of property by fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

Prosecutors established that the Lachman Fire, which he started on January 1, 2025, continued smoldering underground before resurfacing on January 7 as the Palisades Fire. That blaze killed 12 people.

The verdict came at a retrial after his first trial ended in a mistrial. Sentencing is pending.

sources.name: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California

candidates.summary: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck the Banda Sea at approximately 09:42 UTC on November 21, according to GFZ's GEOFON service, which listed a depth of 116 kilometers. Reuters, citing an earlier GFZ estimate, located the earthquake about 226 kilometers northeast of Dili, Timor-Leste.
candidates.title: Magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes Banda Sea northeast of Dili
candidates.geography: Banda Sea, near Timor-Leste and Indonesia

candidates.summary: Negotiations at COP31 continued into November 21 in Antalya after governments failed to reach a comprehensive agreement before the conference's scheduled November 20 close. Outstanding issues included climate finance, emissions reductions, adaptation and a just transition. No final agreement had been reported in the morning coverage; revised negotiating texts remained under preparation.
candidates.title: COP31 negotiations continue beyond scheduled close without final agreement

candidates.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned an assassination attempt against a U.S.-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark and expressed solidarity with Denmark on November 21. She attributed the operation to Russian intelligence services. Reuters reported that Russia's embassy in Copenhagen had said on November 20 that the accusations lacked proof. Von der Leyen said a new European Security Strategy would be proposed; she did not announce its adoption.
candidates.title: Von der Leyen condemns alleged Russian assassination operation in Denmark

candidates.summary: COP31 negotiations remained unresolved on the afternoon of November 21, with no revised negotiating text yet presented, Reuters reported. Countries remained divided over fossil fuels and climate finance after the summit's scheduled November 20 close. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said the outcome would need to be a good deal or no deal. No final agreement had been reported in this coverage.
candidates.title: COP31 remains without agreement as negotiations extend into Saturday afternoon

candidates.summary: An Israeli strike hit a truck carrying food in Gaza City's Tel al-Hawa district on November 21, killing three men, Shifa Hospital director Mohamed Abu Selmiya told the Associated Press. The casualties were taken to his hospital.
candidates.title: Gaza hospital director reports three killed in strike on food truck

candidates.summary: British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting visited Kyiv on November 21. He called for allies to increase support for Ukraine and condemned the previous day's reported Russian airspace violation in Poland. Speaking to reporters before their talks, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reiterated his willingness to attend the December G20 meeting in Miami and hold direct talks with Vladimir Putin there, while noting that Ukraine had not received an invitation.
candidates.title: British defence secretary visits Kyiv as Zelenskyy reiterates readiness for talks
